title: First Day at Coral Reef School
text:
Good morning, little fish! Welcome to Coral Reef School. My name is Mrs. Finley, and I will be your teacher this year.

Class starts when the big shell bell rings. Please swim in a straight line and do not {verb} in the halls. Last year a young crab did that, and he {past tense verb} right into the principal.

In the morning we will learn to read, count bubbles, and swim {adverb}. After lunch, Mr. Inky the octopus will teach art. He has eight arms, so he can paint {number} {plural noun} at the same time.

For snack, please bring seaweed and a little bag of {plural noun}. Our class pet is a {adjective} sea snail named Pudding. She is very shy, so please talk to her {adverb}.

I just know this will be a {adjective} year. Now let's all wave our {plural noun} and say hello!

title: The Diary of Olive the Octopus
text:
Dear Diary,

Today was a busy day. I woke up in my cave and put on all eight of my {plural noun}. That takes a long time when you have eight arms.

For breakfast I ate a bowl of {food} with my best friend, a crab named Nibbles. Then we went to the reef to play hide and seek. I am really good at hiding because I can turn {color}. Nibbles looked for me for {number} hours. He finally found me when I {past tense verb} by accident.

In the afternoon, I helped Grandma Squid in her garden. She grows the most {adjective} {plural noun} in the whole ocean. Then we sat on a rock and watched the whales go {verb ending in ing} by.

Now it is bedtime. I am tucked in with my {adjective} blanket and a {noun}. Tomorrow I will try to {verb} with all eight arms at once.

title: Rules for the Mermaid Library
text:
Welcome to the Mermaid Library at the bottom of Shell Bay. We have over {number} books, and all of them are waterproof. Please follow these rules.

1. Swim quietly. If you need to talk, please whisper like a {animal}.

2. Do not let the sea horses {verb} on the shelves. They are not allowed to check out books until they are {adjective}.

3. Please return your books in one week. If a book is late, the librarian, Miss Coral, will {verb} at you {adverb}.

4. No snacks near the books. The last time someone brought {plural noun} in here, a whole school of fish {past tense verb} into the picture book corner.

5. Story time is every Tuesday. This week Miss Coral will read a book about a {adjective} {noun} who learns to {verb}.

Thank you, and happy reading! Remember, a good book is better than a pile of {plural noun}.

title: Chef Clawdia's Seaweed Smoothie
text:
Hello, ocean friends! I am Chef Clawdia, the best crab cook on the whole reef. Today I will teach you how to make my famous seaweed smoothie.

First, find a big clam shell to use as a bowl. Fill it with two handfuls of green seaweed and one {adjective} {noun}. Next, add a scoop of {food} and {number} tiny {plural noun}. My grandpa always added those, and he was the happiest crab in the sea.

Now it is time to mix. Hold the shell with both claws and shake it {adverb}. If you are a fish, you can ask a friendly octopus to help. While it shakes, you can {verb} nearby.

When the smoothie turns {color}, it is ready! Pour it into a cup and drink it while {verb ending in ing}. It tastes like a {adjective} sock, but in a good way.

My customers say it makes them want to {verb} all day long. Enjoy, and remember to share with your {plural noun}!

title: Meet Grandpa Shelby the Sea Turtle
text:
This week, the Reef Times talked to Grandpa Shelby, the oldest sea turtle in the bay.

Q: How old are you, Grandpa Shelby?
A: I am {number} years old, give or take a week.

Q: What did you do when you were young?
A: I swam all over the world. My favorite place was a beach where the sand was made of {plural noun}.

Q: What is your favorite food?
A: Sea grape jam on toast. Also {food}, but only on Sundays.

Q: How do you stay so healthy?
A: Every morning I like to {verb} for ten minutes and eat a {adjective} breakfast. I also take a long nap inside my {adjective} shell.

Q: What is the secret to a long, happy life?
A: Swim {adverb}, be kind to every {noun}, and never forget to say "{silly word}" to your friends.

Q: Thank you, Grandpa Shelby!
A: You are welcome. Now please excuse me. It is time for me to go {verb ending in ing}.

title: Whale Sings at Ocean Concert
text:
This is Bubbles McFin reporting live from the Deep Blue Concert Hall.

Last night, more than {number} sea creatures came to hear Wanda the Whale sing her new song. Wanda wore a {adjective} hat and a necklace made of {plural noun}. When she began to sing, the whole ocean shook {adverb}.

The crowd loved it. A group of clownfish {past tense verb} in the front row, and a shy jellyfish started {verb ending in ing} in the back. Even the grumpy old lobster said the song made him want to {verb}.

After the show, I asked Wanda where she got the idea for her song. She said, "I was eating a bowl of {food} and thinking about my {noun}." Then she swam away to say hello to her fans.

Wanda will sing again next Friday. Tickets cost one shiny shell and a {adjective} {noun}. Back to you at the news desk!

title: Help Wanted: Jellyfish Night-Light
text:
HELP WANTED at the Deep Dark Trench Hotel!

Our hotel is at the very bottom of the ocean, where it is very dark. Our guests keep bumping into each other on the way to bed. We need a friendly jellyfish to glow in the hallway every night.

The right jellyfish must be able to glow {color} and stay {adjective} all night long. You will also help guests find their rooms. Some guests are very {adjective}, like Mr. Grumble the walrus, who sleeps in a {noun} and asks for {number} pillows.

Other jobs include reading bedtime stories to baby squids, singing softly to the {plural noun}, and reminding Mr. Grumble to {verb} more quietly. You must not be {verb ending in ing} on the job. Last week our old night-light {past tense verb} instead of glowing, and everyone woke up in the wrong room.

Pay is three shells a week and all the {plural noun} you can eat. To apply, please swim {adverb} to the front desk.

title: Postcard from the Yellow Submarine
text:
Dear Aunt June,

Greetings from the bottom of the sea! Dad and I are riding in a yellow submarine with a round window. So far we have seen {number} {plural noun} swim past us.

This morning a curious octopus stuck to the window and stared at my {body part}. Then she waved all eight arms and {past tense verb} away. Dad was so surprised that he dropped his {noun}.

At lunch we parked next to a coral reef. The coral was {color} and looked like a giant {adjective} {noun}. A school of tiny fish swam by {adverb}, and I think they were {verb ending in ing}.

Tomorrow we are going to visit an old sunken ship to look for treasure. Dad says we might also see a {adjective} whale. I hope it wants to {verb} with us.

Love,
Owen

title: How to Throw a Pufferfish Party
text:
Your friend Pip the pufferfish is having a birthday! Here is how to throw the perfect party.

Step one: Send the invitations. Write them on flat shells and tell every guest to bring a {noun}.

Step two: Decorate the reef. Hang seaweed streamers and blow up a bunch of {plural noun}. Do not use real balloons. Pip might think they are his cousins.

Step three: Make the cake. Pufferfish love cake made of sand and {food}. Put a {adjective} candle on top.

Step four: Plan some games. Pip loves to play Pin the Tail on the {animal}. He also likes musical rocks, where everyone has to {verb} until the music stops.

Step five: Get ready for the surprise. When Pip swims in {adverb}, everyone shouts "{exclamation}!" When Pip gets surprised, he puffs up and looks like a giant {adjective} {noun}.

At the end, Pip will be so happy that he {past tense verb} all the way home.

title: Letter to My Pen Pal Coco
text:
Dear Coco,

Thank you for your letter! I loved hearing about your new home in the sea anemone. It sounds very {adjective} and cozy.

Things are busy here in Sandy Cove. Last week my little brother learned how to {verb}. He practices all day long, even at dinner. Mom says he is the most {adjective} starfish she has ever seen.

On Saturday, we went to the Reef Fair. I rode the giant clam ride {number} times and won a prize for {verb ending in ing}. The prize was a jar of {plural noun}. I am saving one for you.

Also, guess what? A sea turtle moved in next door. He is very nice, but every morning he {past tense verb} so loudly that our whole rock shakes. Dad says we should bake him a {noun} to say hello.

Please write back soon and tell me about your {plural noun}. I miss you {adverb}!

Your friend,
Stella
